image_prompt.text: Tall, closely packed low-poly mountains, grass-green on their flanks with white faceted snow caps, rising straight out of a sand floor rippled with small dunes
The tallest snow-capped peak in the range, its white faceted cap standing above the rest so players can orient by it from anywhere in the zone
Sandy routes winding through the narrow valleys between the packed mountains, giving the zone an obvious grain to move along
Composed vantage points on the dunes and lower grass slopes, framing the snowy peaks and the scattered pines behind them
Large angular grey low-poly boulders scattered across the sand and the lower slopes, breaking up the long views between mountains
Sparse low-poly pine trees dotted across the grass slopes and the open sand between the mountains

notes: Stage A is None: this describes a place, not a game type. 'Pet simulator aesthetic' is named as a visual style, so it was not read as a self-declared Simulation genre.
Stage B: there is plainly a space, and a pet-sim style landscape zone reads as ground players move over rather than a diorama the camera orbits, so no SET.

Explorable Place kept intact, but the verticality axis was moved off its default to `tiered` — tall, closely packed mountains are real elevation. No caves, tunnels or overhangs were asked for, so the route is P0 + tiered rather than P2.

Art direction applies to the whole zone rather than to any single pick: colorful, blocky, stylized low-poly cartoon. It has been folded into the wording of every image_prompt entry instead of emitted as an option.

Cannot be built as a layout feature: the request to expose grass color, snow color, tree count, mountain height and zone size as tunable attributes. That is parameterisation of the generated zone, not geometry to place, and belongs to whatever wraps the build.
No counts emitted: 'sparse' trees, 'large' zone and 'tall' mountains are bands rather than stated numbers, and 'tree count' is named only as an attribute to expose.

would have asked: Sounds like an environment showcase — a big stylized landscape with the tallest snow-capped peak as the thing you orient by, sandy routes threading the valleys between the mountains, and a few composed viewpoints, on top of the mountain-and-dune terrain itself. Want that, or would you rather build it up yourself? Judged to fit and taken, since no user was present.
would have asked: Does anyone actually walk this zone, or is it a set the camera looks at? Walkable was assumed; if it is only ever looked at, `SET` is appended and nothing else changes.
would have asked: The large angular grey rocks were read as sightline-breaking scenery (`cover-los`) rather than as plain decorative props — worth one confirmation.
would have asked: Anything else you want in the space? Nothing came back, so nothing was added.
